title: Tithe
subtitle: the men they send
narrative: In April 2019 Wizards previewed Charity Extractor and Tithebearer Giant together on Hipsters of the Coast under the headline 'Behind the Front Lines' — the Orzhov tax cluster. The MTG wiki uses 'indebted spirits' as a literal Ravnica population tier: debtors whose obligations survived their deaths, bound to ghostly labor until the debt is discharged with interest. The Orzhov Syndicate, in canon, is the 'Church of Deals' — religion, banking, and organized crime in one institution. Fifteen cards, twelve names, six sets. The face the institution shows when it comes to collect.

cards.name: Wicked Guardian
cards.why_it_fits: Throne of Eldraine: 'Camelot meets Grimms' Fairy Tales' per Rosewater. 'Wicked' is a deliberate ELD villain-naming convention (Wicked Guardian + Wicked Wolf). She belongs to Locthwain court, whose virtue is Persistence — formally 'persistent efforts at serving the queen.' A noble in purple robes stands upright; a servant kneels behind her scrubbing the stone. The vertical distance is the architecture. 'Some are born to greatness. You were born to scrub greatness's floors.'

cards.name: Charity Extractor
cards.why_it_fits: Co-previewed with Tithebearer Giant in the 2019 Hipsters 'Behind the Front Lines' Orzhov tax cluster. AD Dawn Murin's brief specified a knight on horseback with an offering plate; Matt Stewart cut the horse, replaced the plate with the locked strongbox + keys. For a common he posed himself in armor, sourced horse-armor photos from the Wallace Collection London, used a Christmas ornament for the Orzhov gold. Same artist, same set: his Nicol Bolas mythic-edition oil sold for $35,000.

cards.name: Pitiless Pontiff
cards.why_it_fits: 'Pontiff' is a named Orzhov institutional rank — commands a staff of ministrants, holds direct access to the Obzedat ghost council per the Ravnica sourcebook. Backdrop is Orzhova, the Cathedral Opulent (the 'Church of Deals'). Robed 'Gray Sisters' do all menial labor. The eclipsed-sun signet behind her is the same emblem worn by masters as a medallion and tattooed on slaves as a brand. 'Pay in gold. Pay in blood. Pay with the servitude of your spirit kin. But pay you must.'

cards.name: Mortify
cards.why_it_fits: First printed Guildpact 2006. Twenty-nine printings since, across five distinct flavor texts and six artists. The Anthony Palumbo art carries Hilgur's line — and the Guildmaster's Guide to Ravnica formally defines 'Orzhov euthanist' as 'an assassin euphemistically called a euthanist who brings speedy ends to lives deemed to have gone on too long.' The role was coined as flavor in Guildpact, codified as a job class thirteen years later. 'Your debt is erased.'

cards.name: Tithe Drinker
cards.why_it_fits: Common Orzhov vampire from Dragon's Maze — a set with prerelease attendance ~50% down from Gatecrash, widely considered one of MTG's weakest. Extort was designed by Shawn Main outside the Gatecrash team during devign; MaRo had to draft 14 extort cards to convince skeptics. Same eclipsed-sun signet throne as Pitiless Pontiff above — two masters under one emblem. Slawomir Maniak has 222 MTG cards; this is his only Orzhov-watermark one.

cards.name: Lawmage's Binding
cards.why_it_fits: The first instant-speed Pacifism variant ever printed (Hipsters of the Coast, RNA design review 2019). The Plane Shift: Ravnica supplement canonically describes Azorius magic as 'blue or golden runes floating and glowing in the air in circular patterns or shimmering azure barriers' — the binding ring is house style. Two gauntleted hands restrain a horned figure. The authority is barely in the frame. Just the hands, doing the work.

cards.name: Indebted Spirit
cards.why_it_fits: The MTG wiki uses 'indebted spirits' as a named Orzhov population tier — debtors whose obligations survived their deaths. The card name is a direct lore lift. THE FIRST CARD ever to carry both Bestow and Afterlife. Per a WotC ruling, when bestowed and host die together, you get TWO Spirit tokens from one card — the institution replaces its workers automatically. The skeletal wraith's scroll is the ledger.

cards.name: Charitable Levy
cards.why_it_fits: 'Collection counter' appears on exactly ONE card in the entire Scryfall corpus — this one. The noncreature-tax design lineage runs from Glowrider (Legions 2003) through Thalia, Guardian of Thraben; Charitable Levy is the first ENCHANTMENT version with built-in self-destruct. Fires three times, sacrifices itself, draws a card, tutors a Plains. Charity as tax. The ambient counterpart to Charity Extractor — one visits, one is the weather.

cards.name: Tithebearer Giant
cards.why_it_fits: Co-previewed with Charity Extractor in the 2019 Hipsters 'Behind the Front Lines' cluster. Flavor speaker Teysa Karlov, Orzhov Matriarch, had recently been freed from imprisonment by the Obzedat — punishment for an attempted coup with Boros knight Tajic to expose the Council's corruption. 'I've always said full war chests win wars, but I didn't mean by bashing enemy skulls with them.' The matriarch reads the literal war chest as the wrong tool. The right tool is the abstract one. The tithe.

cards.name: Malevolent Noble
cards.why_it_fits: TV Tropes classifies this card under 'The Bluebeard' — Adaptational Heroism variant. Applies Perrault's 1697 lure-then-kill structure to witches rather than wives, using the witches' own appetite as bait. Eldraine canon makes it credible: the Planeswalker's Guide describes ELD witches as 'shadowy human warlocks who take great joy in their evil deeds' and steal children. 'He has slain a dozen witches, luring each with a promise of fresh children's bones.' The noble in fine clothes IS the predator.

cards.name: Eye Collector
cards.why_it_fits: Per MaRo's ELD design handoff, Rankle is both 'Deal-Making Imp / nod to Rumpelstiltskin' AND the plane's Puck figure from A Midsummer Night's Dream. Eye Collector is his on-the-ground extractor: 'Lord Rankle will see you now—all he asks is a small token of tribute.' Lord, courier, victim. The card waited six years for its first reprint (Foundations Jumpstart 2025) while Rankle himself was reprinted three times — mythic demand vs common neglect. Tribute taken now, your library the next thing it visits.

cards.name: Secure the Scene
cards.why_it_fits: Across ~15 cards Judith the Scourge Diva is quoted on, nearly all carry Rakdos color identity. Secure the Scene (mono-white) appears to be the only outlier — the joke lands because she's the maximally wrong guild-voice to comment on an Azorius arrest. Behind the soldier, a web of luminous blue chains stretches across the sky — official Azorius enforcement visuals per the Plane Shift: Ravnica supplement. The arrest isn't the soldier; it's the mesh of light around him.

pricing.diy_shipping_rate_note: $1.31 matches TCGplayer's standard Plain Envelope rate as of 2026-05-17.
pricing.diy_alternative_note: Fifteen cards across twelve names and six sets (Throne of Eldraine, War of the Spark, Ravnica Allegiance, Dragon's Maze, Core Set 2021, Modern Horizons 3) realistically routes through 6 TCGplayer sellers minimum at $1.31 plain-envelope shipping each. The multi-copy Charitable Levy (2x), Malevolent Noble (2x), and Secure the Scene (2x) often split across sellers too.
pricing.shipping_policy: buyer-paid, itemized separately at checkout; never included in list price
pricing.shipping_rate_note: Matches TCGplayer Plain Envelope rate ($1.31). One envelope, one stamp; we eat the difference if the carrier's actual stamp cost runs over.
pricing.premium_justification: Fifteen cards across twelve names and six sets, weighted toward the Orzhov apparatus-of-extraction thesis. The cards themselves are $2.03 of common bulk; doing this DIY from six TCGplayer sellers at $1.31 plain-envelope shipping each runs $9.89. This lair arrives in one envelope for $5.00 + $1.31. You save the assembly. The lair is what you build with: a thematic binder spread, a thematic deck, a thematic cube — a Lego brick for your own greater curation, organized as such, ready to drop into place.

metadata.notes: v5 recast (2026-05-17 reassessment pass). Dropped Reverent Hoplite (Theros piety, too loose) and Lunarch Mantle (lone inquisitor with relic, too oblique). Replaced with Charitable Levy (2x, MH3 — explicit `tithe`+`taxation`+`extraction` tags, Orzhov enchantment that mechanically embodies the bundle thesis) and Indebted Spirit (MH3 — Orzhov afterlife skeletal ledger-keeper). Then enriched and added three further inventory candidates after vision-pass confirmed thesis fit: Tithebearer Giant (WAR — Teysa-flavored Orzhov giant carrying literal war chest), Malevolent Noble (ELD 2x — bearded noble in spectral-hands doorway, witch-luring villain), Eye Collector (ELD — Lord Rankle's faerie tribute-courier). v4 anchors retained: Wicked Guardian, Charity Extractor, Pitiless Pontiff.
